data.title: Command-Line Parser
data.solution:
from re import search as S,sub
C=open(0).read()
V="[aeiouAEIOU]"*("-y"in C)
i=S("-t\w* (\w+)",C)
j=S("-k\w*( \w+)+",C)
T=sub(V,"",i.group(1))if i else""
K=[sub(V,"",k)for k in j.group().split()[1:]]if j else[]
print(" ".join([f"[{k}]"for k in K if k]+([T]if T else []))or"<BLANK>")
data.statement:
A (fictional) terminal command called {{cdgm}} has the following command-line arguments:

• {{-y}} / {{--yes}}: takes no values.
• {{-t}} [[title]] / {{--title}} [[title]]: specifies a [[title]] value.
• {{--keyword}} [[keyword1]] [[keyword2]] ... [[keywordN]]: specifies [[N]] space-separated [[keyword]] value(s).

These arguments appear <<at most once>> in <<any order>> after the {{cdgm}} command, separated by singular spaces. Values (non-arguments) in the command line will only appear <<directly after>> its corresponding {{-t}}/{{--title}} or {{--keyword}} arguments.

Based on the given command line,

• If {{-y}}/{{--yes}} is specified, remove all vowels ({{aeiou}}, case-insensitive) from every [[keyword]] and/or [[title]] value.
• Discard values that become empty (i.e., that contain only vowels).
• Print remaining [[keyword]](s) in-order as "{{[}}[[keyword]]{{]}}" separated by singular spaces.
• Print the remaining non-empty [[title]] after the keywords, separated by a singular space.
• If there is nothing to print, output {{<BLANK>}} instead.

<<Examples>>
```>> cdgm
<BLANK>

>> cdgm --keyword a b Cdefg --title Spell
[a] [b] [Cdefg] Spell

>> cdgm --yes --title Spell --keyword A B CdEfg
[B] [Cdfg] Spll```

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

A (fictional) terminal command called cdgm has the following command-line arguments:

• -y / --yes: takes no values.
• -t title / --title title: specifies a title value.
• --keyword keyword1 keyword2 ... keywordN: specifies N space-separated keyword value(s).

These arguments appear at most once in any order after the cdgm command, separated by singular spaces. Values (non-arguments) in the command line will only appear directly after its corresponding -t/--title or --keyword arguments.

Based on the given command line,

• If -y/--yes is specified, remove all vowels (aeiou, case-insensitive) from every keyword and/or title value.
• Discard values that become empty (i.e., that contain only vowels).
• Print remaining keyword(s) in-order as "[keyword]" separated by singular spaces.
• Print the remaining non-empty title after the keywords, separated by a singular space.
• If there is nothing to print, output <BLANK> instead.

Examples
>> cdgm
<BLANK>

>> cdgm --keyword a b Cdefg --title Spell
[a] [b] [Cdefg] Spell

>> cdgm --yes --title Spell --keyword A B CdEfg
[B] [Cdfg] Spll





   

      
Input

      
Line 1: A positive integer L; the length of the command line.
Line 2: A L-character string; the command line.

   

   

      
Output

      
Line 1: The required output as per the given command line.

   

   

      
Constraints

      
4 ≤ L ≤ 60
1 ≤ N ≤ 5
Each title and/or keyword is non-empty and only contains English letter(s).

   

   

      
Example

      

         

            
Input

            
18
cdgm --title Hello

         

         

            
Output

            
Hello
